To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the echocardiography-based algorithm for post-Myocardial infarction (MI) left ventricular (LV) thrombus has a high sensitivity (96.3%) for the diagnosis of LV thrombus and a high negative predictive value (NPV) (98.9%) for the exclusion of LV thrombus, which can be used as a gatekeeper for thrombus evaluation by delayed-enhancement cardiac magnetic resonance (DE-CMR).

a) the echocardiographic algorithm for post-MI LV thrombi has a good sensitivity and specificity, and b) the echocardio-graphic algorithm for LV thrombi is a gatekeeper for thrombus evaluation by delayed enhancement CMR.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of new and more efficient numerical methods for the solution of partial differential equations (PDEs), and with the application of such methods to the simulation of complex physical processes.
the development and application of new technologies in cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) for the evaluation and management of heart disease.
the development of a new class of materials, which are based on a new class of compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the echocardiographic algorithm for post-myocardial infarction left ventricular thrombus is a gatekeeper for thrombus evaluation by delayed enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance.
the echocardiographic algorithm for the detection of LV thrombus is a gatekeeper to further evaluation by CMR.
the presence of a left ventricular thrombus is a contraindication for primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we developed a novel algorithm to evaluate post-MI left ventricular (LV) thrombus using 2D echocardiographic data, which can be used to select patients for further evaluation by delayed enhancement cardiovascular magnetic resonance (DE-CMR) imaging.
the ECHO algorithm can be used in the clinical setting to identify patients with LV thrombus.
we have developed an echocardiographic algorithm to screen for LV thrombus in the setting of MI, and that the algorithm has a high specificity for identifying LV thrombus.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a comprehensive, stepwise approach to LV thrombus detection is necessary to avoid misdiagnosis and to optimize the use of CMR for LV thrombus detection in the post-MI setting.
the presence of LV thrombus (LVT) in the setting of myocardial infarction is associated with worse clinical outcomes, and therefore should be considered as an independent risk factor.

echocardiographic assessment of left ventricular (LV) thrombus can be used as a gatekeeper to determine the need for delayed enhancement cardiac MRI (DE-CMR) in post-myocardial infarction (post-MI) patients.
